How to read common Welsh digraphs without overforcing them

Welsh digraphs like CH, DD, LL, NG, RH, and TH each count as single sounds but occupy two letter spaces on the board. This trips up players who treat every two-letter pair as separate entities. A word containing "DD" isn't broken—the DD is one phoneme representing a voiced dental fricative, roughly like saying "this" but softer.

  • DD almost never starts a valid Welsh word but shows up mid-vocabulary regularly

In Welsh, Y is a full vowel with two distinct pronunciations depending on stress and position—it can sound like uh, ee, or even disappear entirely in fast speech. Seeing Y highlighted yellow on the board doesn't mean you've misread anything. It means the word contains that vowel in a position where Welsh allows it.
